- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast slope by 20–40% after sentiment drop.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show high volatility or sentiment extremes, apply “volatility dampening” — reduce forecast variance by 15–30% to avoid overfitting.
